page_note: Hagiographic narrative scene: Mani rises, embraces an elder, kisses him, sits on the bema, and addresses the gathering ('noble ones... free ones who sat before him') asking why they laugh at this old man, in whom the Mind of Light, the Protomē, the Youth/small king, and the beauty of uprightness dwell. Closes with a Gospel citation (Matt 18:10 — 'their angel sees the face of the Father daily'). Substrate vocabulary (Protomē, Youth-king, Mind of Light) is present but deployed in service of editorial pastoral defense of the elect. Page is dominated by apostolic_dialogue narrative + hortatory_application + manichaean_ecclesial (bema, elect, faith, fasting, humility, faithful). Heavy lacunation. Substrate is essentially absent as standalone teaching.
